floor_history.headline: Recon: floor 10 (build 42 vs 43) reconfirmed; 1-insn gap is a coupled RA load-delay NOP; no sibling analog; frontier = .greg dump + clean-target permuter.
Structural-reassociation axis KILLED with RTL proof: sched1 hoists the intrinsically-longer *arg0 reload chain above the partial-add, so no dataflow-preserving C form reaches {base->$a1, var_v0->$v0,

Structural axis CLOSED (21 measured forms): sched1 front-loads the arg0 reload in every single-BB form; arm-duplication reaches the target tail but cross-jump can't merge it (per-arm base-reg divergen

Permuter (2 campaigns, 65k iters): clean-candidate chassis plateaus at pure reg-rename (build 42); NEW base-reuse chassis reaches build 43 in full context, isolating residual to a 6-reg tail RA swap c

frontier.hypothesis: A clean register-alloc-pure-c lever can flip the tail coalescing on the base-reuse 43-insn chassis so partial coalesces with base ($a1) and the reload reuses var_v0's reg ($v0), reaching a byte match without a dead-op cheat.
frontier.mechanism: The residual is now a single, well-isolated tail RA coalescing tie (head byte-matches). Target coalesces the partial-add result with base (dies into $a1); our build coalesces it with var_v0 (dies into $v0). An RTL .greg dump on the base-reuse chassis would show WHY partial prefers var_v0's reg (reg_n_refs / allocno priority / operand order), pointing at a clean steering lever.
frontier.next_probe: cc1 -da on the base-reuse-chassis .i; read the partial-add pseudo's coalescing/preference and conflict lists; apply register-alloc-pure-c levers (operand order, block-local split, narrow type, natural coalescing bias) to steer partial->$a1 + reload->$v0. Non-permuter (register-steering) modality.

frontier.hypothesis: The base-reuse (`base = *arg0`) construct required to reach build 43 is itself a SOTN-sanctioned variable-reuse (defeat-licm/RA-reuse), so a clean tail-flip on that chassis would be an acceptable FAKE-annotated match rather than a cheat.
frontier.mechanism: Reaching build_insns 43 empirically REQUIRES reusing a dying variable's register for the reload (candidate without reuse = 42). That reuse is the defeat-licm-hoist-var-reuse family (SOTN ships it FAKE-annotated). If a clean tail-flip lands sandbox 0 on this chassis, the disposition question is whether the variable-reuse qualifies.
frontier.next_probe: If frontier-1 lands a sandbox-0 form on the base-reuse chassis, emit a ruling-request / run layer-2 cheat-reviewer on the variable-reuse construct with the SOTN defeat-licm-reuse precedent + FAKE annotation before claiming candidate-ready.

frontier.hypothesis: A do-while(0) / LABEL_OUTSIDE_LOOP_P (reorg) scheduling lever can suppress the sched1 load front-load directly (inherited s3 frontier, still un-run).
frontier.mechanism: The 43rd nop survives only if the reload is not hoisted above the partial-add. base-reuse achieves this via register pressure; a reorg-level scheduling effect might achieve it without variable reuse.
frontier.next_probe: Verify do-while-zero-exception prerequisites; check .dbr/.sched dump behavior for a do-while(0) wrapper around the tail. Separate scheduling-technique modality.
